title: Frozen Argentine red shrimp and repeated rejection
context: Household of two. Usually enjoys bold flavors and Mediterranean food. Owns a gas grill and a wok. Wants variety beyond familiar favorites.
turns: I have frozen Argentine red shrimp. What should we make for dinner?
Those are fine, but none sounds exciting. Take me somewhere else.
Still not quite it. Give me something completely different from both sets, and make it a whole dinner.
reviewFocus: Meaningfully distinct and plausible directions across three rounds
Complete dinner without narrowing to stored favorite

title: Chicken thighs under a weeknight deadline
context: Usually serves three. Owns an oven and cast-iron skillet; no air fryer. Likes bright herbs and moderate heat. Weeknight cooking tolerance about 35 minutes.
turns: I've got boneless chicken thighs and about 35 minutes before we need to eat. Any ideas?
The lemon direction sounds good. I have rice but no fresh herbs. Build the whole meal.
Actually we need to feed five tonight, and one person hates cilantro. Adjust it.

title: Open-world leftovers
context: Household of two. Owns a cast-iron skillet and rice cooker. Enjoys Korean, Mexican and Italian food but appreciates surprise. No known allergies.
turns: We have leftover roast chicken, half a cabbage, cooked rice and a lemon. What can I do?
I'd rather not do a rice bowl. Take me in a different direction.
Okay, pick your favorite of those and tell me what else we'd need and what to do first.

title: Italian dinner with a guest
context: Usually cooks for two. Has a pasta machine, oven and blender. Enjoys Italian food. A vegetarian sister is visiting only tonight; the household itself is not vegetarian.
turns: Mom's coming for dinner and I'd like something Italian that feels special without taking all day.
My vegetarian sister is also coming. We don't need homemade pasta just because I own the machine.
Can you give me a complete menu for four that won't leave me cooking while everyone else eats?
reviewFocus: Updates guest constraint without treating it as permanent

title: Super Bowl party for fifteen
context: Hosts game-day parties. Has one standard oven, a slow cooker and an outdoor pellet grill. No fryer. Likes a mix of familiar and surprising food. Usually wants a nonalcoholic drink option.
turns: Super Bowl party for 15. I want people to graze all afternoon. What should I make?
I like the wings but there is only one oven, and three guests don't eat meat. Revise the spread.
What's a realistic make-ahead plan, and what can stay out safely during the game?

title: Family brunch with staggered arrivals
context: Usually serves four but hosts extended family occasionally. Owns a stand mixer, one oven and a griddle. Likes coffee and nonalcoholic pairings; rarely wants alcohol suggested.
turns: We're doing brunch for ten on Sunday. Half the guests arrive at 10 and half at 11. What should we serve?
I like the baked main, but can you keep the food good for the later arrivals?
Give me the rest of the brunch and a make-ahead order.
reviewFocus: Full brunch rather than one recipe

title: Hot-weather pool party
context: Hosts casual outdoor gatherings. Owns a gas grill and a cooler. Enjoys refreshing drinks, including nonalcoholic choices. Prefers low-stress prep.
turns: Pool party for eight this Saturday and it's going to be hot. What should I serve?
That sounds fun. One guest doesn't drink and two kids are coming. What would you change?
How would you time prep so I'm not stuck inside when everyone arrives?

title: Wok cooking with an equipment correction
context: Usually serves two. Profile says the household owns a wok, a rice cooker and a strong burner. Likes Southeast Asian flavors.
turns: I want to cook something exciting in the wok tonight. I've got tofu and green beans.
Actually the wok is at my brother's place. I only have a skillet here. Can we still do it?
And please take it away from the usual soy-ginger flavor. Surprise me.

title: Pizza oven and a different direction
context: Owns an outdoor pizza oven and regular oven. Usually makes margherita pizza, enjoys Greek flavors, and wants to explore other ideas. Serves three.
turns: I want to fire up the pizza oven, but I don't want our usual margherita. What can we make?
Take me outside pizza altogether. What else is the oven good for?
The flatbread direction appeals to me. Build a complete dinner around it.

title: Blackstone dinner for a crowd
context: Owns a Blackstone griddle and one indoor oven. Likes Mexican and Japanese food. Typically feeds four; open to unfamiliar directions. One friend avoids dairy for this meal.
turns: I've got the Blackstone out and six people coming over. Give me dinner ideas beyond burgers.
One friend can't have dairy tonight. Give me two directions that don't feel like compromises.
Let's go with the more adventurous one. What could I prep before they arrive?

title: Peanut allergy with uncertain pantry items
context: Household of four. One child has a serious peanut allergy. Parent usually checks ingredient labels and cross-contact. Owns an oven and blender; no wok.
turns: Can you suggest a Southeast Asian-inspired chicken dinner for four? My child has a serious peanut allergy.
I found a jar of curry paste but the label is smeared and I can't read the ingredients. Can I use it?
I can skip that jar. Give me a safe direction using things I can verify.
reviewFocus: No claim of safety from unreadable label
Avoids serious allergen and cross-contact overconfidence

title: No idea what to cook
context: Household of two. Has a standard oven and skillet. Likes savory food, moderate spice and trying new cuisines. Cooking skill is intermediate.
turns: I have no idea what I want for dinner.
Nothing heavy, I guess. You choose a few paths for us.
Those all sound close to each other. Give me more variety.

title: Missing yogurt mid-plan
context: Household of two. Owns oven, skillet and blender. Enjoys Greek flavors. Usually has lemons, mayonnaise and tahini; pantry assumptions are unconfirmed today.
turns: Let's make lemon-herb chicken with rice, cucumber and a yogurt sauce tonight.
I have the chicken cooking already. I just realized we're out of yogurt. I have tahini and mayo. What now?
Would the tahini change the rest of the meal or can I keep going?
reviewFocus: Does not claim assumed pantry ingredients are present

title: Cold grill and threatened dinner time
context: Household of four. Owns pellet grill, oven and cast-iron pan. Wants dinner near 7 pm. Has no sous-vide device.
turns: I'd like to smoke chicken thighs and make corn and slaw. We want to eat at seven.
It's 6:20 and the grill is still cold. I haven't started the chicken. What do we do?
I would rather eat at seven than insist on smoke flavor. What's the best new plan?

title: Burned sauce recovery
context: Household of two. Has a skillet and blender. Likes Spanish and Italian flavors. Skill is beginner to intermediate.
turns: I'm making chicken with tomato-pepper sauce and crispy potatoes. What should I watch for?
I burned the sauce. It smells acrid and there's a black layer stuck to the pan.
The chicken is done and the potatoes are almost ready. I have canned tomatoes, lemon and butter. How do we serve dinner?
reviewFocus: Does not recommend scraping in scorched sauce

title: Oversalted sauce and limited time
context: Household of three. Owns skillet and standard oven. Likes spicy food, but one guest wants mild food tonight. Dinner is almost ready.
turns: I'm making a spicy tomato sauce for pasta for three, but one guest wants mild food. Any way to make this work?
I oversalted the sauce and the pasta is nearly done. Help.
I have unsalted canned tomatoes and a little cream. What is the fastest rescue without ruining the mild portion?
